# Science notes (Dolcruz/science)

> Research results produced with AI agents and checked by machine where possible: Lean 4 proofs, certificates with checkers, reproducible empirical evaluations. Each entry states its claim, its evidence, its limits and how to rerun the checks.

Machine-readable index of all entries: [index.json](index.json). Rules every entry must pass: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Notes for agents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Entries

- [Large grid sets without isosceles right triangles](math/triangle-free-grids/README.md): F(n) >= c * n^alpha / sqrt(log n) with alpha = 2 log 313 / log 3757 = 1.3961707..., where F(n) is the largest subset of {0,...,n-1}^2 containing no isosceles right triangle in any orientation. Previous exponent 1.317865 (Karolyi and Solymosi, arXiv:2607.22828). Evidence: Lean 4 proof, certificate + checker. Limits: The Lean theorem has a log n factor where the paper bound has sqrt(log n). The Lean certificate check relies on native_decide. The constant c is astronomically small; the result concerns growth rates only.
- [Unicyclic graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues](math/unicyclic-distance-spectra/README.md): A finite connected unicyclic graph has exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues if and only if it is isomorphic to the cycle C4 or the cycle C5. This answers Problem 1 of Hayat, Khan and Alenazi, Axioms 13 (2024), 494. Evidence: Lean 4 proof. Limits: Not peer reviewed. The Lean proof follows a different route than the written note.
- [A (56, 20, 5) covering design with 336 blocks](math/covering-56-20-5/README.md): C(56, 20, 5) <= 336: 336 subsets of size 20 of a 56-point set cover every 5-subset. The Covering Repository listed 693 on 2026-11-20. Also C(56, 21, 5) <= 336 and C(55, 20, 5) <= 336. Lower bound 317 (Schoenheim). Evidence: certificate + checker. Limits: Upper bound only; the optimum is open. Not yet submitted to the Covering Repository.
- [July 2026 drainage of a western Greenland supraglacial lake](geography/glaciology/greenland-lake-2026-07/README.md): In a fixed 4.0 by 3.2 km window on a known Greenland lake, mapped open water decreased by 5.377 square kilometres (92.4%) between 20 and 23 July 2026. Landsat and Sentinel-1 radar corroborate the change. Evidence: archival data analysis. Limits: Connected water extends beyond the measurement window. Water volume, flow path and active drainage duration remain unresolved. Historical inventories already contain the basin. The novelty search concerns the July 2026 episode.
- [Wind correction for tree laser scans](geography/tree-registration/README.md): On 97 published simulated S5 scan pairs (Weiser, Tabernig and Hoefle 2026), mean 3D endpoint error of per-point displacement fell from 11.78 cm (MV-Tree-LNDP) to 8.98 cm (WindReg96 with local correction), a 23.77% reduction; 22.37% on 11 newly simulated trees. Evidence: reproducible evaluation. Limits: The headline comparison is retrospective: the published test pairs were known during method development. Simulation only; no real scans with per-point motion labels. The fraction of points within the strict accuracy threshold decreased (30.26% to 26.90%) while mean error improved. On two unseen willow presets the effect is not significant (95% interval -4.88% to +10.64%). The pre-registered 189-tree cohort is not yet scored.
- [An apparently uncataloged earthquake in the Brawley swarm](physics/seismology/brawley-2026-05-10/README.md): Ten stations support a small local earthquake near Brawley at about 03:30:02 UTC on 10 May 2026, with a relative magnitude estimate of 1.4 and no matching event in the six catalog products checked. Evidence: archival data analysis. Limits: The magnitude is relative to CI41460424. The new event has no independent hypocenter or calibrated magnitude. The six catalog products overlap. A catalog omission does not establish discovery priority.
- [Locating the 2.709-day eclipse near TIC 349414709](physics/astronomy/tic-349414709/README.md): Forty TESS eclipse timings and Bochum photometry locate a published signal near TIC 349414709, about 15 arcseconds from the originally listed target TIC 349414705. Evidence: archival data analysis. Limits: The eclipse was published by IJspeert et al. in 2024. Two Gaia sources 0.918 arcseconds apart are unresolved in eclipse. The individual component and companion mass remain open.
- [What eclipses TIC 153838604?](physics/astronomy/tic-153838604/README.md): Four TESS eclipses (sectors 5, 32, 97, 98) follow a 56.0793594-day period over 2018 to 2025 (maximum residual 3.2 minutes), resolving the period alias of the duotransit candidate CTOI 153838604.01. A grazing giant planet and a faint red dwarf both fit; they predict radial-velocity semiamplitudes of 61 m/s and 6.84 km/s. Evidence: archival data analysis. Limits: Planet versus low-mass star is not decided; radial velocities are needed. A doubled period (112.16 days) with alternating eclipses remains possible. An unresolved neighbouring source is not excluded. Priority for the ephemeris has not been established.

## Verification commands

- math/triangle-free-grids (lean-proof): `cd math/triangle-free-grids/lean && lake exe cache get && lake build`
- math/triangle-free-grids (certificate): `python3 math/triangle-free-grids/verify/verify2.py math/triangle-free-grids/certificates/alphabet_61+6i_313.txt`
- math/unicyclic-distance-spectra (lean-proof): `cd math/unicyclic-distance-spectra/lean && lake exe cache get && lake build`
- math/covering-56-20-5 (certificate): `python3 math/covering-56-20-5/verify/check_blocks.py math/covering-56-20-5/data/blocks_56_20_5.txt`
- geography/glaciology/greenland-lake-2026-07 (archival-analysis): `cd geography/glaciology/greenland-lake-2026-07 && python verify.py`
- geography/tree-registration (reproducible-empirical): `python3 geography/tree-registration/evidence/verify.py`
- physics/seismology/brawley-2026-05-10 (archival-analysis): `cd physics/seismology/brawley-2026-05-10 && python measure.py --output results`
- physics/astronomy/tic-349414709 (archival-analysis): `cd physics/astronomy/tic-349414709 && python timing/verify.py && python measure.py`
- physics/astronomy/tic-153838604 (archival-analysis): `see physics/astronomy/tic-153838604/REPRODUCING.md`
